languages.name: French
languages.alphabet: Latin (26 letters + accents: é è ê ë à â ù û ü î ï ô ç)
languages.description: French is an official language in 29 countries and is the language of art, cuisine, diplomacy, and culture.
languages.fun_fact: French gave English around 10,000 words, including 'café', 'ballet', and 'entrepreneur'.

languages.name: German
languages.alphabet: Latin (26 letters + umlauts: ä ö ü ß)
languages.description: German is one of the most spoken languages in Europe and a major language of science, philosophy, and engineering.
languages.fun_fact: German has very long compound words — 'Donaudampfschifffahrtsgesellschaft' means 'Danube steamship company'.

languages.name: Spanish
languages.description: Spanish is the second most spoken language in the world by native speakers and is growing rapidly.
languages.fun_fact: Spanish has two words for 'to be' — 'ser' for permanent states and 'estar' for temporary ones.

languages.name: Arabic
languages.alphabet: Arabic script (28 letters, written right to left)
languages.description: Arabic is the liturgical language of Islam, spoken across the Middle East and North Africa.
languages.greeting: مرحبا (Marhaba — Hello) / السلام عليكم (As-salamu alaykum — Peace be upon you)
languages.fun_fact: Arabic gave us words like algebra (al-jabr), alcohol, coffee, and cotton.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin)
languages.alphabet: Chinese characters (Hanzi) — thousands of characters; Pinyin romanisation for pronunciation
languages.description: Mandarin Chinese has more native speakers than any other language on Earth.
languages.greeting: 你好 (Nǐ hǎo — Hello) / 早上好 (Zǎoshang hǎo — Good morning)
languages.fun_fact: Chinese is a tonal language — the same syllable spoken in different tones has completely different meanings.

languages.name: Japanese
languages.alphabet: Three scripts: Hiragana (46), Katakana (46), and Kanji (thousands of characters)
languages.description: Japanese is known for its politeness levels, unique writing systems, and cultural richness.
languages.greeting: こんにちは (Konnichiwa — Hello) / おはよう (Ohayou — Good morning)
languages.fun_fact: Japanese has no plural forms — you say 'one cat', 'five cat' (not 'five cats').

languages.name: Korean
languages.alphabet: Hangul — 24 letters arranged into syllable blocks, invented in 1443
languages.description: Korean is one of the most logical alphabets ever created and was designed to be easy to learn.
languages.fun_fact: Hangul was invented by King Sejong the Great specifically to reduce illiteracy in Korea.

languages.name: Russian
languages.description: Russian is the most widely spoken Slavic language and an official UN language.
languages.fun_fact: Russian has no word for 'the' or 'a' — articles simply don't exist in Russian.

languages.name: Italian
languages.alphabet: Latin (21 letters — no j, k, w, x, y in native words)
languages.description: Italian is the language of opera, art, fashion, and some of the world's greatest cuisine.
languages.fun_fact: Italian is the closest living language to Latin, the language of the Roman Empire.

languages.name: English (Advanced)
languages.description: English is the global lingua franca — the world's most studied second language and the language of science, technology, and international business.
languages.greeting: Hello / Good morning / How do you do?
languages.fun_fact: English borrows from over 350 languages — around 60% of English words come from French and Latin.

languages.name: Portuguese
languages.alphabet: Latin (26 letters + accents: á â ã à é ê í ó ô õ ú ç)
languages.description: Portuguese is the official language of nine countries and the fifth most widely spoken language in the world, with the largest number of speakers in Brazil.
languages.fun_fact: Portuguese and Spanish share about 89% of their vocabulary, making them among the most closely related major world languages.

languages.name: Turkish
languages.alphabet: Latin (29 letters; special characters: ç ğ ı i ö ş ü)
languages.description: Turkish is an agglutinative language, meaning it builds meaning by adding suffixes to a root word. It is the most widely spoken Turkic language and bridges Europe and Asia.
languages.fun_fact: In Turkish, the entire sentence 'Are you one of those people who cannot be Czechoslovakianised?' can be expressed in a single long word: Çekoslovakyalılaştıramadıklarımızdanmısınız?

languages.name: Persian (Farsi)
languages.alphabet: Persian script (32 letters, written right-to-left; based on Arabic script)
languages.description: Persian is one of the world's great literary languages, with a tradition of poetry stretching back over a thousand years. Poets such as Rumi, Hafez, and Omar Khayyam wrote in Persian.
languages.greeting: سلام (Salâm — Hello) / صبح بخیر (Sobh bekheyr — Good morning)
languages.fun_fact: Persian was the lingua franca of large parts of the Middle East and South Asia for centuries, influencing Arabic, Turkish, Urdu, and Hindi with thousands of borrowed words.
